title: GLTF importer: Backface culling re-import does not update in editor while scenes open
body: ### Tested versions I bisected the dev releases and found a regression in 4.4-dev4. Issue persists in latest beta of 4.7. - Reproducible in: 4.4-dev4, 4.4.1, 4.6.2, 4.7-beta1 - Not reproducible in: 4.3, 4.4-dev3 ### System information Godot v4.7.beta1 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9636) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description Say that you have a GLTF mesh loaded in the editor in an open scene, and it has a material with `"doubleSided":true` (which corresponds to `cull_mode = CULL_DISABLED` in the imported StandardMaterial3D). If you change the GLTF file, setting `"doubleSided":false` or removing it entirely (as `false` is the default), and re-import (either implicitly or explicitly), you would expect to see `cull_mode = CULL_BACK`. However, the change will not be reflected in the editor (either visually, or in the property inspector) until _all_ scenes involving that material are closed and re-opened. This _eventually_ resolves (when closing all scenes and re-opening, or restarting the editor). Does not affect the running project, only the editor. Curiously, this bug does not happen the other way around (changing `doubleSided` from `false` to `true` is instantly reflected in the editor). While this is only an editor bug, it is extremely confusing because `doubleSided:true` is the default set by Blender. So it is quite likely for a user (such as myself) to first export with the defaults, then turn on backface culling in Blender, re-exporting and importing, and become confused as to why it is still disabled in Godot. This is even a suggestion in an official [Godot tutorial](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/importing_3d_scenes/available_formats.html#:~:text=To%20resolve%20this%2C%20enable%20Backface%20Culling%20in%20Blender%27s%20Materials%20tab) - anyone following the advice of "enable Backface Culling in Blender's Materials tab, then export the scene to glTF again" will run into this issue. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a new Blender project with the default cube. In Edit mode, select one face and delete it (so that we can easily see inside the cube, to test if backface culling is working). 2. Export to GLTF. (File > Export > GLTF; change Format to "glTF Separate" so we can inspect the text file.) Note that the GLTF file includes the line `"doubleSided":true` in the material, which is the default in Blender. 3. In a new Godot project, import the cube GLTF file. Add it to a 3D scene. Note that you can see the insides of the cube (correct). 4. Now either: a) in Blender, select the cube, go to Material (red ball icon), Settings > Surface > Backface Culling and check "Camera", and re-export. Or, b) in a text editor, edit the GLTF file and delete the line `"doubleSided":true`. (These are equivalent - we are turning on backface culling so we expect the inside faces of the cube to become invisible in Blender's Material Preview mode, and in Godot.) 5. Go back to Godot (with the 3D scene still open) and allow auto-import, or explicitly import by right-clicking the GLTF file > Reimport. Note that you can _still_ see the insides of the cube (**incorrect**). Note that if you open the cube scene, in the inspector: Mesh > Surface 0 > Material > Transparency, `cull_mode` is incorrectly set to `CULL_DISABLED` when it should now have changed to `CULL_BACK`. (This is not just visual - the data has not updated.) 6. Close either of the scenes (the 3D scene with the cube, or the cube scene itself) and re-open them. The bug persists as long as one scene remains open. 7. Close all scenes then open the 3D scene again (or restart the editor). The bug is now gone: the inside faces of the cube are invisible and the material's `cull_mode` is properly set to `CULL_BACK`. This is what it looks like with backface culling disabled (correct behaviour for Step 3, but wrong after Step 5): This is what it looks like with backface culling enabled (expected behaviour after Step 5): ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [backface-update-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27265654/backface-update-bug.zip) This is at Step 3 in the above repro steps (since the remaining steps must be done in a single editor session to trigger the bug).
